transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-01-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 mins
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Verdance - Head of ML), Jonas Reed (Verdance - Platform), Sara Liu (Verdance - Security)

Summary:
Short kick-off to understand Verdance's plan to move off OpenAI for core product generation and evaluate options (Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private). They run a mix of API and self-hosted vLLM for cost reasons. Main concerns: parity on outputs, latency, tokenization differences, KMS, and an enterprise procurement timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer. How are you Maya, Jonas, Sara?
[00:10] Maya: Doing good, thanks. We're excited but also, you know, cautious. We've been running production on OpenAI for the last 9 months and—there's a lot to untangle.
[00:20] Priya: Totally, and congrats on scaling. What are the immediate pain points? Cost, latency, control?
[00:30] Jonas: Cost and the black box feeling. We run a bunch of batch jobs with vllm on prem and some latency-critical endpoints on OpenAI. The big ask is: can Redwood mirror our current latency SLOs and output quality, and what breaks when we change tokenizers or quantize?
[00:45] Alex: Good, so two parallel threads: functional parity (quality/regression) and infra fit (latency & ops). On parity—what model families are you using? Are you on GPT-4 style APIs or Claude-like?
[00:58] Maya: We're primarily on OpenAI GPT-4o for generation and using small Claude-2 for some assistant tasks. Also running Llama-2-13b quantized on vLLM for internal tools.
[01:12] Priya: Ok so a mix. When you say 'run Llama-2-13b on vLLM', is that on-prem GPU clusters? And what's your tokenizer mismatch risk—are you doing prompt engineering that relies on exact token offsets?
[01:27] Jonas: Yes, on-prem clusters, Kubernetes. Token offsets matter for our snippet extraction; we've had subtle shifts moving between TGI and vllm, like off-by-one token splits, which causes some downstream matching to flake.
[01:42] Sara: For security, we need SSO (SAML), KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, and audit logs. Also data residency for EU customers—we need EU-only processing for certain tenants.
[01:55] Alex: All standard asks. Redwood Private does customer-managed VPC and on-prem connectors, KMS/HSM integrations, and we can document SOC2 artifacts. For EU residency, we can pin region routing and restrict models to region-specific pools.
[02:10] Maya: From a parity standpoint, we ran a small eval where Redwood's hosted model produced more repetition on long-form completion compared to OpenAI, any recs?
[02:20] Priya: We usually see that differences come from decoding defaults and tokenizer differences. We can match temps/top_p and also provide model-specific sampling profiles. Also, Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and batching configs without regressing quality—this is where an eval set helps.
[02:36] Jonas: Can you run an A/B with our eval set? We want to see not just log-prob metrics but downstream metrics (like entity extraction F1) and edge-case prompts.
[02:46] Alex: Absolutely. Typical PoC: you provide 10-50 representative prompts and expected outputs, we run parity sweeps across hosted/dedicated/private variants and share a regression report. We can also run a throughput test on your sample traffic.
[03:00] Sara: On encryption, do you have in-transit and at-rest covered? And keys—can we bring our own keys?
[03:08] Priya: TLS for transit, AES-256 for rest, and yes BYOK through KMS/HSM integrations. For Redwood Private we support customer keys, and for Dedicated we have optional KMS link ups.
[03:20] Maya: Procurement-wise, timeline is tight—finance wants a vendor with an enterprise contract by end of Q1. We'll need pricing and compliance docs.
[03:32] Alex: We'll send a two-path pricing: hosted per-token with committed discounts and a dedicated reserved capacity quote with monthly commits. Also include private licensing terms.

-- TIMESTAMPED DISCUSSION (more verbatim, with transcription artifacts) --
[03:45] Jonas: One weird thing we saw was vllm mem growth after a long prefix cache, is that something Redwood handles with automatic KV pruning?
[03:55] Priya: Yes, we have KV cache eviction policies and continuous batching that trims KV when we hit thresholds. Sometimes it's tuned per workload—like very long-context summarization needs a different policy.
[04:10] Jonas: Hmm okay. When you say 'continuous batching', do you mean requests are batched cross-tenant? We can't have cross-tenant mixing.
[04:18] Priya: No, not mixing. Batching is tenant-isolated. The runtime opportunistically aggregates within the same customer pool to improve GPU utilization.
[04:30] Maya: For evaluation, how do you handle deterministic vs non-deterministic outputs? We need repeatability for tests.
[04:38] Priya: We can run deterministic sampling (fixed seeds / greedy) for eval parity. For production, you can choose stochastic decoding. Our eval harness preserves randomness controls.
[04:48] Sara: Logs: can we get request-level audit logs for every generation including input, model version, and token counts? We require 12 months retention for certain customers.
[04:58] Alex: Yes, we have configurable retention. For Private you can set retention policies and export logs to your SIEM. For hosted, we provide logs with retention up to X days by default and extended retention as an add-on.
[05:12] Maya: What about model pinning during rollouts? We want to canary a new quantized variant in dedicated before flipping prod.
[05:22] Priya: Rollouts are supported: canary, A/B, automatic fallbacks. You can pin model versions at route-level. We also have automated regression alerts tied to your eval sets.

[05:40] Jonas: Tokenization mismatch—if we move from OpenAI to a Redwood-curated LLM, how do you help map tokens? We have a lot of prompt templates.
[05:50] Priya: We provide tokenizer diff reports and a migration guide per model pair. In many cases it's whitespace splitting differences; we can suggest prompt rewrites and sampling configs.
[06:05] Maya: Costs—what's the delta going from OpenAI usage at scale to Redwood Hosted? We need a TCO with dedicated reserved capacity scenarios.
[06:15] Alex: We'll build a TCO doc. Short answer: hosted is competitive, but for sustained high throughput dedicated reduces per-token cost via reserved GPU amortization.

[06:30] Sara: Any compliance red flags? If we need FedRAMP down the road, is Redwood on that path?
[06:38] Alex: We're SOC2 and have enterprise controls; FedRAMP is a bigger lift—it's not on our immediate roadmap but we can discuss third-party hosting options and dedicated on-prem splits for that compliance.
[06:52] Jonas: For the PoC benchmarking—can you run vllm/TGI parity? We want to see if TGI fast-chat style optimizations map over.
[07:00] Priya: We can. We'll include runs on both vLLM and TGI-style runtime variants. Small note: names sometimes get mis-typed in tools—vllm vs v-L-L-M—our docs cover that.
[07:12] Maya: On the product side, if we need to call external tools or function-calling, does Redwood support structured output and tool calling?
[07:20] Priya: Yes, streaming + function calling + structured outputs supported—payloads include model-confidence and token usage headers.
[07:32] Sara: Any SLA for latency? We need a P50/P95 target, especially for synchronous endpoints.
[07:40] Alex: For hosted we publish latency profiles per model; for Dedicated we can guarantee P95 under the reserved capacity contract and include SLOs in the SLA.

[07:55] Maya: Ok, what's the usual PoC length? We were thinking 2-4 weeks.
[08:02] Alex: Typical is 2-6 weeks depending on breadth. For you, with eval parity and perf tests, 3 weeks seems feasible—week 1 onboarding and dataset ingest, week 2 parity runs, week 3 tuning & final report.
[08:18] Jonas: Are there any known gotchas moving prompts that rely on stop-token heuristics?
[08:24] Priya: Stop token behavior can vary by runtime; we'll run stop-token normalization in the harness.
[08:32] Maya: Okay great. One more question—billing granularity. If we burst beyond reserved capacity, how is that handled?
[08:40] Alex: There's burst capacity options and overage billing; we'll include that in the quote. Dedicated pools have burst to shared capacity subject to policy.

[08:52] Sara: Also need to know about access controls—RBAC, SSO, and audit trail for model deploys.
[08:58] Priya: RBAC is route and project scoped; we integrate with SAML SSO and can log deploy events.

Recap / Next Steps:
[09:10] Alex: Recap: Verdance will share a set of 10 eval prompts + expected outcomes and sample traffic profile. Redwood will send: pricing (hosted + dedicated + private), compatibility checklist, and a PoC plan with timelines. Priya will prepare vLLM/TGI parity notes and a sample runbook.
[09:30] Maya: We'll try to get the prompts and traffic slice by Monday.
[09:36] Jonas: Procurement is target end of Q1 so we'll need to move fast.

Action Items:
- Alex: Send pricing + reserved capacity options and compliance docs by 2026-02-02

- Maya: Provide evaluation prompts (10-20) and sample traffic profile by 2026-02-01
